MythosMini is a small language model ("mini Fable") built in Python 3.12. This file is the contract for any agent working here. Read it fully, then read `journal.md` before starting any task. Detailed procedures live in `docs/rules/` — read the relevant one before doing that kind of work; they are part of this contract, not optional extras.

Alright, the user wants me to train the model for roughly a minute, observe the tokens‑per‑second (tps) metric, then dig into the agents contract (AGENTS.md) and diagnose why the throughput isn’t in the tens of millions tps and fix it—without killing any running processes.

I’ve already launched a training run with a 75‑second timeout (the `timeout 75 python3 train.py …` command) and set up a background monitor to wait for the process to finish. I also tried a quick `until ! pgrep -f "python3 train.py"` loop to know when it ends. While the training is still running (or maybe just finished), I need to locate where the code actually reports the tps value so I can see what numbers are being printed, and later I can tweak whatever is limiting the throughput.

My first attempt was a broad grep across the whole `src/` tree and the top‑level `train.py` for strings like “tok/s”, “tokens_per”, or “tps”. That only returned two hits:
- A URL in `src/mythosmini/config.py` (irrelevant)
- Two lines in `src/mythosmini/training/loop.py` that compute `tokens_per_step` and `total_steps`.

So the actual progress reporting isn’t in `loop.py`. I suspect the library has a dedicated telemetry or progress‑bar module that prints out metrics during training. Looking at the repository tree from the earlier `ls` output, I saw a `src/mythosmini/telemetry` package, which likely contains the progress bar implementation. Indeed, the name `progress.py` suggests it handles live stats like steps, loss, and throughput.

Therefore, the logical next step is to inspect that file for any occurrence of token‑related terminology. I’ll search for word boundaries around “tok” (to catch “token”, “tokens”, etc.) and also patterns like “/s” (common in “tokens/s”) or “rate”. Using `grep -rn "tok\b\|/s\|rate"` will recursively list line numbers and matches, and piping to `head` will give me a quick snapshot without flooding the output. Additionally, to get a sense of the file’s size (maybe it’s split across multiple functions), I’ll run `wc -l` on both `progress.py` and `loop.py` so I know how many lines each contains—useful for later navigation or when I need to edit the file.

This combined command will give me exactly the information I need to pinpoint where the tps metric is generated, without modifying anything yet. It aligns with the user’s request to “look at the tokens per second” and sets me up for the subsequent diagnosis and fix.

Hence I’ll issue the following Bash tool call:
`grep -rn "tok\\b\\|/s\\|rate" src/mythosmini/telemetry/progress.py | head; wc -l src/mythosmini/telemetry/progress.py src/mythosmini/training/loop.py`
